consumer_seed: The Ofcom mobile switching guide was published on 1 October 2016.
The Ofcom mobile switching guide was last updated on 1 July 2026.
Ofcom says mobile customers can switch provider using Text to Switch.
Text to Switch uses a free text message.
A mobile customer does not need to speak to the current provider to use Text to Switch.
Texting INFO to 85075 checks mobile contract status and possible early termination charges.
A customer who wants to keep the mobile number can text PAC to 65075.
A customer who wants a new mobile number can text STAC to 75075.
The current provider must reply with a PAC or STAC within one minute.
A PAC or STAC switching code is valid for 30 days.
The switching response must include information such as early termination charges.
For pay-as-you-go customers, the switching response must include the credit balance.
Accounts with more than one number must request PAC or STAC by phone or on the provider website.
After the new provider receives the PAC or STAC, the mobile switch must complete within one working day.
A cancelled mobile customer can request to keep the old number for free within one month of cancellation.
The Ofcom broadband switching guide was published on 4 August 2010.
The Ofcom broadband switching guide was last updated on 1 July 2026.
Under One Touch Switch, the customer contacts the new broadband provider and it arranges the switch.
Ofcom notes that switching broadband can save money for customers who are out of contract.
Ofcom notes that broadband bundled with landline or mobile may reduce costs.
Changing broadband provider before contract end may trigger early termination charges.
One Touch Switch tells the customer about applicable early termination charges.
The new broadband provider needs details of the services being switched.
The One Touch Switch request includes the customer's address.
The One Touch Switch request includes the name of the current provider.
If details match, the current broadband provider sends information to help the customer decide whether to proceed.
The new broadband provider arranges the switch for the preferred date where possible.
The old broadband service ends automatically once the new service is working.
The old provider must not charge for a notice period after the broadband switching date.
Any broadband loss of service during switching must not last longer than one working day.
A broadband switching order can be cancelled within 14 calendar days.
The Ofcom landline switching guide was published on 27 February 2017.
The Ofcom landline switching guide was last updated on 1 July 2026.
Under One Touch Switch, the new landline provider arranges the switch.
Changing landline provider before contract end may trigger early termination charges.
One Touch Switch tells the landline customer about applicable early termination charges.
A landline switching request can state whether the customer wants to keep the phone number.
The current landline provider sends information to help the customer decide whether to proceed.
The old landline service ends automatically once the new service is working.
The old provider must not charge for a notice period after the landline switching date.
Any landline loss of service during switching must not last longer than one working day.
One Touch Switch does not apply when the customer manages the switch and cancellation separately.
A cancelled landline customer can request to keep the phone number for free within one month of cancellation.
A landline switching order can be cancelled within 14 calendar days.
The Ofcom broadband universal service guide was published on 8 August 2023.
The Ofcom broadband universal service guide was last updated on 19 June 2026.
Every UK home and business has a legal right to request a decent, affordable broadband connection.
A decent connection is defined as at least 10 Mbit/s download speed.
A decent connection is defined as at least 1 Mbit/s upload speed.
Eligible applicants request an upgraded connection from BT, or KCOM in the Hull area.
An applicant does not need to be an existing BT or KCOM customer.
BT or KCOM has 30 days to confirm eligibility and the estimated connection cost.
Eligibility requires no access to an existing decent broadband service.
Eligibility also requires no planned public broadband scheme coverage in the next 12 months.
A customer whose only decent service costs more than £59.60 per month can request a universal service connection.
If the connection share costs £3,400 or less, the applicant does not pay for the build or upgrade work.
Most universal service connections are expected within 12 months, though some can take up to 24 months.
